channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Russia launches ~4,000 strikes on Ukraine in a week: at least 8 killed, dozens injured
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says nearly 4,000 drones, aerial bombs and missiles were fired in one week; the conflict touches the main source of Uzbekistan's remittances.

item.title: Uzbekistan wins the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand
item.description: Uzbekistan's open team took gold on home soil in Samarkand with 20 match points and first place — the nation's second Olympiad title.

item.title: Pakistan and Afghanistan on the brink of open war: dozens killed, border shut
item.description: September strikes and clashes have killed dozens and now threaten Uzbekistan's $7 billion Trans-Afghan railway.

item.title: The US F-1 student visa: how it works, step by step
item.description: What the F-1 academic student visa is and how it differs from M-1 and J-1; the steps from admission (Form I-20) to visa issuance (the $350 SEVIS I-901 fee, DS-160, the $185 visa fee, the interview); the proof-of-funds requirement; work rules (20 hours/week on campus, CPT, 12 months of OPT, a further 24 months for STEM); duration of status (D/S) and the 60-day grace period; and F-2 dependents. Based on the US Department of State, USCIS, and ICE (SEVP), as of September 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration gains sweeping powers and immunity
item.description: A new constitutional law grants the administration broad powers, makes its head deputy chair of the Security Council, and guarantees lifetime immunity to senior officials.

item.title: Mustafa Chokay and the Turkestani political emigration (1917–1941)
item.description: The life and émigré history of Mustafa Chokay (1890–1941), a leader of the Turkestan (Kokand) Autonomy: the autonomy proclaimed in November 1917, its suppression in February 1918, his route Baku–Tbilisi–Istanbul–Paris into France, the journal “Yash Turkestan” printed in Berlin 1929–1939 (117 issues), his stance in the Second World War, and his death in 1941. The Promethean movement and other Turkestani émigrés. Verified facts only; disputed details are flagged.

item.title: A tragedy in Namangan reignites Uzbekistan's death-penalty debate
item.description: After a case involving a five-year-old girl, Presidential Administration head Saida Mirziyoyeva called for applying the death penalty; rights defenders stress it will not return.

item.title: How US health insurance works: the basics for immigrants
item.description: The US has no single universal public system — coverage is a mix of employer-sponsored insurance, the individual marketplace (ACA/HealthCare.gov), and public programs (Medicaid, Medicare). Key terms: premium, deductible, copay, coinsurance, and the annual out-of-pocket maximum ($10,600 for an individual in 2026). The ACA Marketplace, subsidies, and metal tiers; Medicaid and the five-year waiting bar; Medicare (65+); emergency care and EMTALA; in- vs out-of-network (HMO and PPO). Based on HealthCare.gov, CMS, Medicaid.gov, and KFF (as of 2026).

item.title: Israeli Finance Minister Calls for a 'Gaza-Style' War in the West Bank
item.description: Bezalel Smotrich also demanded dismantling the Palestinian Authority; Cairo and the Palestinians condemned the remarks.

item.title: Uzbekistan's international recognition and UN membership (1991–1992)
item.description: How the world recognized Uzbekistan after the declaration of independence (31 August 1991): Turkey first (16 December 1991), the USA (25 December 1991), the CIS (Alma-Ata, 21 December 1991), UN membership (2 March 1992, on the same day as seven other former Soviet republics), and the IMF and World Bank (21 September 1992). Sourced history with exact dates.

item.title: Court Jails Taftish Journalists and Former State Security Officers: Up to 10.5 Years
item.description: The case was heard in a closed military court; no official information was released. Charges: slander, insult, fraud and extortion.

item.title: How exchange rates are set and why they change: a full reference
item.description: Exchange-rate regimes (free and managed float, fixed/peg), the drivers that move a rate (supply and demand, interest rates, inflation, the trade balance, capital flows), nominal vs real rates, and purchasing power parity (the Big Mac Index). With Uzbekistan's case: the 5 September 2017 liberalization (4,210 → 8,100 som/dollar) and the som's rate today. Based on the IMF and the Central Bank of Uzbekistan.

item.title: Amid the Truce, an Israeli Drone Strike Kills One and Wounds Seven in Gaza
item.description: Gaza's Government Media Office says the ceasefire has been violated 4,379 times; the truce took effect in October 2025.

item.title: US naturalization (N-400): the process, the test, and the oath
item.description: How a lawful permanent resident (green-card holder) becomes a US citizen: eligibility (5 or 3 years), the N-400 application and fee, the English and civics tests (a new 128-question version from 20 October 2025), the Oath of Allegiance, and the dual-citizenship question. A reference based on USCIS — not legal advice.

item.title: Assistant Prosecutor Detained Taking a $4,700 Bribe in Tashkent Region
item.description: Prosecutors say $12,000 was demanded in total. The person is presumed innocent until proven guilty by a court.

item.title: Russian Strikes Kill at Least Four in Ukraine; Trump Urges a Deal
item.description: Casualties in Zaporizhzhia and Sumy; injuries in Kyiv. About 10 people were reported killed in strikes by both sides that day.

item.title: The Uzbek community in Russia: how labor migration formed
item.description: From Turkestan's incorporation into the Russian Empire (1865–1873), through Soviet-era internal movement, to the mass labor migration after independence — how the Uzbek community in Russia took shape. Figures: in 2024 Russia supplied 77% of Uzbek remittances ($11.5bn); the patent system (2015), the 2021 census (323,278), and recent restrictions. Sourced history.

item.title: Tajikistan Considers Withdrawing From the International Criminal Court
item.description: The lower house reviewed a draft resolution on 16 September; the trigger is the ICC warrant against Putin.

item.title: Israel's Elections Committee Bars All Arab Parties From the Knesset Vote
item.description: The decision, made before the 27 October election, must be approved by the High Court, which has overturned such bans before.

item.title: Pakistan Strikes 10 Sites Inside Afghanistan; At Least 4 Civilians Killed
item.description: After strikes hit Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces, cross-border gunfire continued along the frontier.

item.title: Iran Offers 7-Day Plan to Reopen Strait of Hormuz; Trump Rejects It
item.description: Iran's foreign minister set out the conditions; the US president rejected the proposal and said the naval blockade would stay.

item.title: Uzbek labor migration to South Korea: history and the EPS system
item.description: The history of Uzbek labor migration to South Korea: from the flawed 1990s Industrial Trainee System to the state-run EPS (Employment Permit System) launched in 2004; the EPS-TOPIK test, the E-9 visa, the numbers and the turning points. Fact-based, sourced history.

item.title: How to detect disinformation and fake news: a practical guide
item.description: The difference between disinformation, misinformation and malinformation; IFLA's 8-step checklist; the SIFT method; reverse image search; signs of deepfakes; fact-checking organizations — a fact-based media-literacy guide grounded in authoritative sources.

item.title: ICT Week Uzbekistan 2026: 300+ Companies From 51 Countries Gather in Tashkent
item.description: The 22–25 September event focused on artificial intelligence, startups and the venture capital market.

item.title: 29 December 1991: the independence referendum and first presidential election
item.description: On 29 December 1991 Uzbekistan held two votes on a single day: a referendum confirming independence (98.26% in favor) and the first direct presidential election (Islam Karimov 87.14%, Muhammad Solih 12.49%). Sourced history with exact dates and figures.

item.title: How the US tax return works: basics for immigrants
item.description: What a US income tax return is, who must file, the difference between an SSN and an ITIN, Form 1040 and W-2, the April 15 deadline, refunds and penalties — a fact-based guide for immigrants from Uzbekistan, based on IRS sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan's state symbols: how the flag, emblem and anthem were adopted
item.description: How and when independent Uzbekistan's three state symbols were adopted: the State Flag on 18 November 1991; the State Emblem on 2 July 1992; the State Anthem on 10 December 1992. The meaning of each, what the colors and symbols stand for, and who created them. A facts-based, sourced history.

item.title: Russian Drone Hits 16-Storey Building in Central Kyiv: 14-Year-Old Killed
item.description: At least 7 people were injured in the 25 September morning strike; Ukraine's president said 282 drones were launched overnight.

item.title: What inflation is and why prices rise: a full guide
item.description: Inflation is a general, sustained rise in prices and a fall in the purchasing power of money. How it is measured (the consumer price index), its types and causes (demand, cost, money supply), the difference between nominal and real income, and how the central bank controls it. A facts-based, sourced guide, using data from the Central Bank of Uzbekistan and the IMF.

item.title: World Bank: Uzbekistan's Poverty Fell From 17% to 5.8%, Middle Class Roughly Doubled
item.description: 3.7 million people left poverty in 2021–2025; but most new jobs are informal and prosperity is uneven across regions.
